tip.probability: In how many of the 31 weather scenarios this option is the fastest. The higher, the safer the choice.
tip.confidence: Share of scenarios that put the boat in the same area at that time. It drops over time: the weather gets less certain.

how.lead: Paste your position: the router finds the best route on the game's weather and on 31 variants of it, then gives you up to 3 options with their probability and the orders to enter.
how.stat.step: precision of orders over the first 6 hours
how.flow.title: In short
how.flow.1.title: Your position
how.flow.1.text: Paste the position from the game, pick your boat and your next mark.
how.flow.2.title: The weather
how.flow.2.text: The game's wind (GFS) and 31 scenarios (GEFS), over 5 days.
how.flow.3.title: The routes
how.flow.3.text: One optimal route per scenario, with your sails and options.
how.flow.4.title: Your advice
how.flow.4.text: Up to 3 options, their probability and the route plan, order by order.
how.data.title: The data
how.data.gfs.title: The game's weather
how.data.gfs.text: The 0.25° GFS model used by Virtual Regatta, read as the game does: 10 m wind every 3 hours, interpolated in between, over 5 days.
how.data.gefs.title: 31 scenarios
how.data.gefs.text: The same forecast run 31 times with small variations, at 0.5°, every 3 hours. This is what measures uncertainty.
how.data.polar.title: The boat's polar
how.data.polar.text: The boat's speed for each wind strength and angle, for each of the 7 sails, with the foil, hull and winch bonuses.
how.data.course.title: The course
how.data.course.text: For each race: start line, gates and marks to round, finish line and exclusion zones, taken from the official sailing instructions.
how.data.geo.title: Coasts and depths
how.data.geo.text: Public-domain coastline and depths, to avoid land and draw the chart.
how.fresh.title: Weather updates
how.fresh.lead: NOAA publishes 4 forecasts a day. The game picks each one up about 3 h 40 after its nominal time, and so does the site. The times below are in your time zone.
how.fresh.background: Nothing to watch: the site checks every 10 minutes, downloads new forecasts and recomputes your last request in the background.
how.fresh.kept: A result is kept until the weather changes: same position, boat and settings, and it shows at once.
how.route.title: How a route is computed
how.route.caption: Each dotted line joins the points reachable at the same time: an isochrone.
how.route.1.title: Try every heading
how.route.1.text: From your position, a heading every 1°, over 110° on each side of the direction of the mark aimed at. For each, the wind forecast at that place and time gives the speed with your fastest sail.
how.route.2.title: Move step by step
how.route.2.text: 15 min steps until +6 h, 30 min until +24 h, 1 h until +48 h, then 3 h. Tacks, gybes and sail changes cost the time you set.
how.route.3.title: Avoid land and zones
how.route.3.text: Any track crossing an exclusion zone or passing within 1 nm of the coast is dropped: our coastline is not exactly the game's, the margin avoids running aground in the game. Near course gates, only the real coast counts. Marks to round are left on the required side.
how.route.4.title: Keep the best
how.route.4.text: In each direction, the point furthest towards the mark is kept. Repeat up to 5 days, then trace the path back.
how.options.title: Options and probabilities
how.options.lead: A forecast can be wrong. So a route is computed for each of the 31 scenarios, and those passing the same place at +24 h and +48 h are grouped. Each group becomes an option, 3 at most.
how.options.probability.title: Probability
how.options.probability.text: The share of scenarios in the group: 16 out of 31 gives 52 %. If they all go the same way, there is a single option.
how.options.recommended.title: Recommended option
how.options.recommended.text: The most probable one. "Set now" shows its heading, sail, wind and speed.
how.options.game.title: Game weather
how.options.game.text: This badge marks the option containing the route computed on the game's exact weather.
how.options.plan.title: Route plan
how.options.plan.text: One line per change of heading or sail, to the minute, with the confidence: the share of scenarios passing there.
how.settings.title: Your settings
how.settings.sails: Game sails and options (foils, hull, pro winch): tick what you own, the route only uses that.
how.settings.maneuvers: Maneuver times pre-filled with the game's values, editable by hand.
how.settings.polar: You can import your boat's polar from the game; otherwise the community polar is used.
how.settings.marks: The next mark is found automatically; for a mark to round, such as an island, pick it yourself.
how.limits.title: What the tool does not do
how.limits.advice: It does not play for you: you enter your orders in the game.
how.limits.horizon: No arrival time: beyond 2 to 3 days the weather becomes uncertain. Recompute with each new forecast.
how.limits.game: The game may differ slightly: its coastline and the detail of its penalties are not published.
how.limits.polar: The community polar may differ slightly from the game's.
how.sources: Sources: NOAA NOMADS (GFS, GEFS) · official sailing instructions · Virtual Regatta polars · Natural Earth · Leaflet · leaflet-velocity
how.limits.energy: No skipper energy: in the game, a tired skipper manoeuvres up to twice as slowly (twice as fast when fully rested). Here manoeuvre times are fixed: avoid chaining manoeuvres when your energy is low.
polar.title: Polar and options
polar.lead: Tick or untick a game option to see what it changes on the boat's speed, then measure its effect on your route. Your settings are not changed unless you decide so.
polar.chart_label: Polar: boat speed by true wind angle
polar.options.title: Options to try
polar.options.lead: The "yours" badge marks what is ticked in your settings. The pro winch does not change speed: it shortens manoeuvres, its effect shows on the route.
polar.summary.none: Tick or untick an option to compare with your settings.
polar.summary.same: At {tws} kn, these options do not change speed.
polar.summary.gain: At {tws} kn: up to {best} % at TWA {twa}°, {mean} % on average between 40 and 160°.
polar.keep: Keep these options in my settings
polar.kept: Settings updated: the next route computation will use them.
polar.impact.title: On your route
polar.impact.lead: Computes the route on the game's weather with your settings, then with the ticked options, from your last position, and compares the distance to go.
polar.impact.no_position: No position yet: compute a route on the map first.
option.outlook.tip_recommended: Distance still to go to the finish, through every mark, averaged over the 31 weather scenarios.
option.outlook.tip_other: Miles ahead (+) or behind (−) the recommended option, averaged over the 31 weather scenarios, as distance to go to the finish through every mark.
option.outlook.tip_row: {when}: ahead in {ahead} of {total} scenarios, at worst {worst} nm
